Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
Must is unstressed when it is a plain obligation (I must go) and stressed when it corrects (you MUST read it). Have to reduces to /hæftə/, and mustn't keeps a full /ʌ/ in careful speech.
Read it aloud, then record yourself: the main stress falls on the content word, not on the hedge.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Permission, Obligation and Prohibition.

Obligation comes in two kinds: must and have to for what is required, with must usually expressing the speaker's authority and have to an external rule. Prohibition is must not or is not allowed to; don't have to and needn't mean no obligation at all, which is the opposite. Read the rule from two directions: is the action required or optional, and who decided it. In contracts, shall carries the obligation and may carries the permission, and neither is decorative.

must — obligation from the speaker: you must submit the form today
have to / has to — obligation from outside: staff have to wear badges
must not / be prohibited from — prohibition: visitors must not photograph the exhibits
needn't / don't have to — no obligation: you needn't book in advance
may / be allowed to — permission: you may use the archive on request
shall / is to be — formal requirement in documents: the contractor shall complete the work by June
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'You ___ bring a laptop; one is provided.'
2. Complete: 'Visitors ___ not touch the display.'
3. Which verb carries obligation in a contract?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

Permission — You may use the archive on request. (Formal permission.)
Obligation — You have to register first. (External rule.)
Prohibition — You must not remove the files. (Absolute ban.)
No obligation — You don't need to print it. (Optional.)
What do you observe?
The same obligation changes strength with its source: must imposes, have to reports, must not forbids, needn't releases. Read each example for who decided.
1. Does 'you mustn't' mean 'you don't have to'?
2. Which form marks an external rule rather than the speaker's authority?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can explain rights and obligations.

Success criteria:
- I can tell obligation from prohibition from no obligation.
- I can choose must or have to by who decided.
- I can use shall and is prohibited from in formal rules.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ You mustn't pay; entry is free (prohibition where no obligation is meant) → ✅ You don't need to pay; entry is free
❌ You must to submit the form (modal followed by to) → ✅ You must submit the form
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

Bags must not be left unattended.
The lessee shall maintain the premises.
You don't need to copy me in.
